- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.3) and forecast is overly conservative, slightly increase the lower bound to avoid underestimating rebound.  
- If the last 3–5 days of history show a strong upward trend, model tends to overreact — apply a 3–5 day lag correction by smoothing the forecast curve downward.  
- When sentiment is neutral (0.3–0.7) and forecast diverges from true outcome by >3%, apply mean reversion: adjust forecast toward recent 7-day average.  
- For forecasts with high volatility (e.g., >10% swing in 30d), reduce confidence in early-term predictions — especially if sentiment is mixed or trending sideways.  
- If true outcome consistently exceeds forecast by 2–5% over 3–5 days, model underestimates momentum — increase forecast by 1–2% per day for the next 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment is consistently high and forecast is flat or declining, reverse the trend slightly — even if historical data suggests continuation.
